ai.description: This lizard grows to 20 cm. It is olive-brown with a dark nuchal stripe and a pale lateral band. Distinctive features include three prominent, serrated dorsal crests and a white patch on the throat.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura tricarinata* is best distinguished by the presence of three distinct, prominent longitudinal ridges (keels) running along its back, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Tricarinate forest agama inhabits humid, mossy broadleaf forests and shrublands across the Himalayas at elevations ranging from approximately 1,500 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The tricarinate forest agama is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks to camouflage itself against predators until the last possible moment.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura tricarinata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Tricarinate forest agama occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, spanning Northeast India (Sikkim, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh) at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
